coverageMatrix.completeness: Doxycycline provides essentially complete coverage of the single causative organism.
gaps: None for the primary pathogen - coverage gaps would only arise from a missed alternative diagnosis.

stewardship.deescalation: Not applicable - doxycycline is already the single most targeted agent. If the patient fails to defervesce within 48-72 hours, reconsider the diagnosis rather than escalating antibiotics.

drugs.drug: Azithromycin (pregnancy, young children, or doxycycline intolerance)
drugs.coverage: Effective alternative in situations where tetracyclines are relatively contraindicated.
Historic alternative, generally reserved given hematologic toxicity concerns; doxycycline remains preferred even in severe disease.

framework: Do not withhold empiric doxycycline while awaiting serology in a clinically compatible presentation - early treatment dramatically reduces morbidity and the response itself supports the diagnosis.

Doxycycline is not contraindicated for short courses even in children when scrub typhus is suspected, per current guidance, given the risk of untreated disease - this is a common point of unnecessary hesitation.
Treat the full 7-day course even after the characteristic rapid defervescence, to ensure complete clearance.
